title: Car Detailing Cost Per Lead 2026: Google, LSA and Meta
summary: A click on car detailing costs $3.27 on average in the US. See cost per lead at 5%, 10% and 15% conversion, Google vs Meta, and a monthly ad budget formula.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- **Click prices:** A click on car detailing averages $3.27 in the US, mobile detailing averages $3.48, and ceramic coating averages $6.54.
- **Per lead:** At a 10% conversion rate, the $3.27 car detailing click works out to $33 per lead ($3.27 / 0.10 = $32.70). At 5% it is $65, and at 15% it is $22.
- **Facebook and Meta:** LocaliQ's 2026 all-industry figure is $27.39 per Meta lead against $66.69 per Google search lead. Meta leads cost less, but Google searchers are already looking for a detailer.
- **Starting budget:** Jobs you want, divided by your booking rate, times your cost per lead. Start on one channel and adjust after a month of real data.


## What a click costs


These are the main searches car detailing customers use, with what a click costs at the top of Google in the US.


Search Searches a month (US) Average click Top of page range


car detailing 135,000 $3.27 $1.69 to $6.11


mobile detailing 27,100 $3.48 $2.07 to $7.50


ceramic coating 60,500 $6.54 $1.78 to $10.00


The spread inside each row is wide because three things move the price. Urgency matters: someone who wants a car cleaned before a sale or an event will pay more attention to the first ad they see, and advertisers bid for that moment. Competition matters: ceramic coating is a bigger job than a standard detail, so more shops bid on it and the average click is about twice the other two. City matters most of all, because a dense metro with dozens of detailers pushes the top of the range up, while a smaller town sits near the bottom.


## From click to cost per lead


A click is not a lead. Cost per lead is the click price divided by the share of clicks that turn into a call, form or message. The table uses the $3.27 average click on car detailing. The last column is an example only: it assumes 1 in 3 leads books a job, so cost per booked job is the cost per lead times 3.


Conversion rate Cost per lead Cost per booked job (example: 1 in 3 books)


5% $65 ($3.27 / 0.05 = $65.40) $196 ($65.40 x 3 = $196.20)


10% $33 ($3.27 / 0.10 = $32.70) $98 ($32.70 x 3 = $98.10)


15% $22 ($3.27 / 0.15 = $21.80) $65 ($21.80 x 3 = $65.40)


The same click price can produce a lead that costs three times as much, depending on the page, the offer and how fast you answer. To run your own click price and conversion rate through the same math, use the[cost per lead calculator](https://www.sprites.ai/tools/cost-per-lead-calculator) .


## Google Ads vs Local Services Ads vs Facebook for car detailing businesses


How you pay Intent When it wins for car detailing


Google Search ads Per click, set by auction High: the person typed the service they want When you want bookings now, and when you can split campaigns by job such as interior detail, mobile detailing and ceramic coating


Local Services Ads Per lead, with the price set by Google by category and area High: the person is looking for a local provider When Google offers them for your service and area, since you stop paying for clicks that never call


Facebook and Instagram (Meta) Per impression or click, often with a lead form Lower: the person was scrolling, not searching When the job sells on how it looks: before and after photos, ceramic coating, and maintenance offers to past customers


Local Services Ads work differently from search ads. Google charges per lead and sets the price by category and area, so there is no fixed price to quote here. Google decides which job types get the format, and car detailing is not a category to assume is available in your area. Check what the sign-up shows for you, and read the[guide to Google Local Services Ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) before you plan around them. Where they are offered, they win on risk: you pay when a lead arrives, not when someone taps.


For benchmarks, LocaliQ's 2026 figures for automotive repair, service and parts, a related industry and not car detailing itself, show a Google search cost per lead of $29.96, an average click of $4.35 and a conversion rate of 15.51%. LocaliQ's 2026 all-industry averages are $66.69 per Google search lead and $27.39 per Meta lead. Meta is less than half the Google figure per lead, but that gap says nothing about which leads book more often. See the[average cost per lead by industry](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/average-cost-per-lead-by-industry) for how these compare across trades.


## How much to spend each month


Use one formula: **jobs you want / booking rate x cost per lead = monthly budget.**


Here is an example with stated inputs. Say you want 20 booked jobs a month, and 1 in 3 leads books (an example rate, so swap in your own). That needs 20 / (1/3) = 60 leads. Using the 10% conversion cost per lead of $32.70 from above, the budget is 60 x $32.70 = $1,962 a month. If your page only converts at 5%, the same 60 leads cost 60 x $65.40 = $3,924, which is why fixing conversion comes before raising spend.


Start on one channel, usually Google Search for the main detailing job, and run it for a month before adding another. Two channels at once split your budget and make it hard to tell which one produced the bookings. The[car detailing advertising guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/car-detailing-advertising) covers how to set up that first campaign.


## How to lower your cost per lead


- **Make one clear offer.** A named package, such as interior and exterior detail with a booking slot this week, converts better than a general promise to detail cars.
- **Send each search to a matching page.** Someone searching mobile detailing should land on a page about mobile detailing, with your service area, a phone number and a short form at the top. Give ceramic coating its own page, since its click costs about twice as much.
- **Answer fast.** Detailing customers message several shops. Reply to calls and forms within minutes, and set up an automatic text for missed calls.
- **Add negative keywords.** Block searches from people who are not buying, such as jobs, training, courses, supplies, products and DIY, so you stop paying for those clicks.
- **Tighten your service area.** Target the zip codes or radius you actually drive to. A click from outside your area costs the same and never books.
- **Ask the right questions on the form.** Vehicle make and model, the service wanted and the zip code let you quote quickly and filter out poor fits. Keep it short, because every extra field lowers conversion. To see what car detailing businesses run on Facebook, browse the[car detailing ad examples](https://www.sprites.ai/car-detailing-ads) .
